title: Major Cloud Provider Outage — Customer Communication & Remediation Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines how Customer Success (CS), Support, SRE, and Product coordinate communications and remediation when a major cloud provider outage (AWS/GCP/Azure) materially impacts customer-facing services: Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated fleets, and customer Private deployment control planes. The goal is to: 1) notify affected customers clearly and quickly, 2) provide actionable remediation steps and timelines, and 3) preserve trust by documenting impact and follow-up actions.

Scope and impact criteria:

- Severity threshold to use this playbook: any single-region or multi-region cloud provider incident that causes one or more of the following for a customer or customer cohort for > 10 minutes: 
  - API error rate (5xx) >= 5% above baseline AND sustained for 10+ minutes,
  - p95 token latency >= 2x normal baseline for 15+ minutes,
  - inability to reach customer’s Dedicated pool or Private control plane (network/DNS/peering failures),
  - customer-reported total disruption for production traffic.

Roles and responsibilities:

- CS Lead (owner): coordinate customer notifications, approve messaging templates, own post-incident outreach.
- SRE Lead: provide incident timeline, mitigation steps, and ETA for service restoration.
- Support Triage/Oncall: apply severity label, update incident in Zendesk/Jira, route customer tickets.
- Product/Infra: identify and execute cross-region failover or capacity changes; own rollback/compatibility decisions.
- Legal/Compliance (if impacted customers are regulated): review communications for regulated data language.

Escalation matrix (high-level):

1) Detection: Monitoring alerts or customer reports -> Support routes to SRE incident channel.
2) Classification: SRE assigns P2/P1. If P1, CS Lead and Eng Director paged immediately.
3) Execution: SRE executes mitigation; CS drafts initial customer communication within 20 minutes.
4) Live updates: CS updates every 30–60 minutes until incident is resolved, then daily during root-cause analysis (RCA) for 72 hours.

Detection signals and runbook triggers:

- Monitoring signals (any single signal can trigger further investigation):
  - Control-plane API 5xx rate > 5% (10m window).
  - Ingress error rate (LB) > 3% and sustained 10m.
  - Region-specific cluster heartbeats missing for 2+ checks.
  - Customer Private deployment heartbeat failure (customer-ping TTL miss x3).
  - Telemetry: sudden spike in retry/backoff traces from customers.

Immediate CS actions (first 60 minutes):

1) Assemble facts: affected regions, services, customer list (use customer-impact dashboard), estimated impacted percent of requests.
2) Use the template below to send an initial targeted notification to affected customers within 20 minutes (see templates).
3) Open/annotate a dedicated ticket for each impacted customer; tag with incident ID and severity.
4) Offer recommended short-term mitigations: region fallback, reduced throughput mode, or temporary model variant with lower resource pressure.

Customer-facing notification templates (use verbatim and fill placeholders):

- Initial short notice (channel: in-product banner + email + account Slack):

Subject: [Redwood] Service disruption in {REGION} affecting {PRODUCT} 

Hello {CUSTOMER_NAME},

We are investigating a cloud provider outage in {REGION} that is impacting {PRODUCT} (Hosted API / Dedicated pool / Private control plane). Our engineers are actively working on mitigation. At this time we estimate {IMPACT_ESTIMATE}.

What we’re doing:
- Triage and mitigation with our SRE and Infrastructure teams.
- Exploring cross-region failover and capacity re-allocation where possible.

What you can do now (recommended):
- If you can, switch traffic to {ALTERNATE_REGION} (see instructions below).
- If you are on Dedicated, request a temporary burst allocation via your account manager.

We will send an update by {NEXT_UPDATE_TIME}. You can track progress at {STATUS_PAGE_LINK} or reply to this message.

— The Redwood Team

- Follow-up status update (every 30–60 minutes): include incident ID, latest ETA, and any actions customers should take.

Technical remediation options (actionable steps):

- For Hosted API customers:
  - Option A: Automatic region fallback (if eligible): SRE verifies model compatibility and re-routes traffic to {ALTERNATE_REGION} using traffic-routing policy. Typical time: 15–45 minutes.
  - Option B: Rate-shedding & degrade mode: recommend reducing max tokens or switching to a lower-memory model variant. CS should provide pre-approved configuration snippets.

- For Dedicated customers:
  - Option A: Provision emergency burst capacity in a healthy region (Requires finance approval for cross-billing if outside committed capacity). Estimated lead: 30–90 minutes.
  - Option B: Apply temporary routing to sibling Dedicated pools (if peered). Provide customer the routing token and TTL.

- For Private deployments:
  - Option A: Work with customer network ops to failover peering or update DNS TTLs; share our prescriptive commands and TTL guidance.
  - Option B: Provide remote-run troubleshooting support: collect controller and agent logs, coordinate with customer NOC.

Operational runbook snippets (examples):

- Find impacted customers (CLI):

  # Query internal customer-impact dashboard (example)
  redwoodctl incidents list --region {REGION} --impacting true --output csv

- Initiate cross-region fallback (SRE only):

  # Trigger traffic policy change
  redwoodctl routing promote --from-region {REGION} --to-region {ALTERNATE_REGION} --models "gpt-xx*" --dry-run=false

Communication timeline matrix (responsibilities):

| Time window | CS | SRE | Support | Product | Notes |
|-------------|----|-----|---------|---------|-------|
| 0–20m | Send initial targeted notice | Begin triage and mitigation | Tag tickets | Support diagnosis | Initial fact-gathering |
| 20–60m | Send update (targeted) | Execute short mitigations | Open per-customer tickets | Validate model compatibility | Offer workarounds |
| 1–6h | Broader status broadcast | Cross-region failover or capacity changes | Route escalations | Coordinate billing/credits if needed | Hourly updates |
| 6h+ | Owner: CS Lead prepares post-incident plan | Continued recovery and RCA | Keep customers informed daily | Approve remediation credits | Prepare QBR/RCAs |

Severity to customer SLA / credit guidance (example):

- If customer experiences unavailability > 99.9% monthly for a billable product in a paid environment, follow the Enterprise SLA credit workflow. CS prepares a provisional credit estimate and routes to Finance/Legal.

Post-incident follow-up and QBR material:

- 72-hour post-incident: share timeline, root cause summary (high-level), mitigation steps, and planned long-term fixes.
- For enterprise customers, include a dedicated QBR slide with: incident timeline, customer impact metrics (requests affected, error rates, cost of mitigation), proposed technical changes, and a remediation commitment with dates.

RCA checklist items to include in customer communications:

1) What happened (plain language)
2) Why it happened (high-level vendor or configuration cause)
3) What we did to mitigate and when
4) What we will change to avoid recurrence
5) Any customer action still required and timelines

Escalation examples (scenarios):

- Scenario A: Multi-region cloud outage affects Hosted API globally — action: declare P1, enable automatic region routing, send company-wide customer bulletin, offer account credits for impacted customers.
- Scenario B: Single-region outage affecting a small set of Dedicated pools — action: targeted notices, provision burst capacity, and schedule one-on-one account calls where needed.
- Scenario C: Private customer control-plane unreachable due to cloud peering change — action: CS-led immediate coordination call with customer NOC and our Infra; provide runbook for DNS/peering rollback.

Metrics and postmortem deliverables:

- Include the following in the post-incident artifacts (to be shared with impacted customers where appropriate):
  - Incident ID, start/resolve timestamps, services affected, percent of customer traffic impacted, mitigation steps and timestamps.
  - Customer-specific request/error counts and latency curves (attach CSV).
  - List of follow-up engineering tasks and owners with ETA (format: JIRA-12345: title -> owner -> target date).

Appendix: quick templates and links

- Internal Slack channel naming: #incident-{INCIDENT_ID}-{region} (ops-created).
- Status page URL placeholder: {STATUS_PAGE_LINK} (replace with status.redwood.ai/incidents/{INCIDENT_ID}).
- Billing/credit contact: finance-credits@redwood.ai (for CS to CC).

Related pages and references:
